properties.title: ICare-DT: a digital twin for continuous forecasting of intensive care patients

membership.reason: ICare-DT is a causally masked Transformer ICU digital twin that continuously assimilates hourly observations into latent state z_t without retraining for 1-48h competing-risk forecasting and next-hour action-conditioned rollout.
membership.counting_boundary: Verified L2 action-conditioned/continuous-assimilation ICU world model (WT_EHR, BP_FORECAST).

properties.backbone: Causally masked Transformer over 161 hourly channels (41 physio, 120 treatment) + masks + competing-risks/endpoint/rollout heads

properties.flow: Hourly ICU record H_t -> frozen-weight Transformer state synchronization z_t -> 1-48h competing-risk forecasts, clinical endpoints, and next-hour rollout

properties.purpose: Continuous online ICU forecasting and treatment-response testbed.
properties.environment: Harmonized eICU-CRD (201k), MIMIC-IV (94k), MIMIC-III (28k) + semi-synthetic washout benchmark

assertions.rationale: Explicit hourly measurement masks across 161 channels.
Harmonized eICU-CRD, MIMIC-IV, and MIMIC-III onto unified 161-channel hourly grid.
Causally masked Transformer encoding physiology, labs, treatments, masks, and static covariates.
Persistent latent patient state z_t updated hourly.
State synchronization re-reads newly arrived hourly measurements with frozen weights without retraining.
Conditioned on causal patient history H_t.
120 explicit treatment channels and next-hour chosen action rollout head.

An action-conditioned next-hour counterfactual rollout adapter is implemented, but it was evaluated only on an earlier historical semi-synthetic benchmark (Fig. 4a) where an earlier model version had a rollout clock defect, trailed predicting zero effect (MAE 0.021 vs 0.017), and the authors explicitly state no positive finding rests on those readouts (pp. 3, 9-10, 31, 68). Retained at implementation stage; does not establish L2.

Evaluated 1-48 h competing-risks future vital-sign crossing forecasts across 12 settings on eICU-CRD test stays (+0.073 to +0.153 AUROC over hour-6 forecasts) and transferred without refitting to MIMIC-IV (8/9 settings, +0.025 to +0.114 AUROC), though gradient boosting was stronger on validation and MIMIC-IV beat last-value in only 1/9 settings (pp. 1, 3-5, 23).
Continuous ICU patient forecasting and treatment-response benchmarking.
1-48h vital-sign crossing competing-risks AUROC (+0.073 to +0.153 over hour-6 baseline).
Semi-synthetic washout benchmark testing known individual treatment effects; documents out-of-support failure of standard learners.
Withheld/swapped-hours controls trace forecast gains specifically to the patient's own new measurements.
Prespecified external transfer to MIMIC-IV (8/9 settings) and cross-era MIMIC-III.
Explicitly audits observation-process / measurement-time visibility of treatment effects.

evidence_fragments.content:
treatment responses, but few studies test whether routine records support either. We propose
ICare-DT, a Transformer-based twin that updates a latent patient state hourly from new mea-
surements without retraining. We trained it on 140,473 eICU-CRD stays to forecast vital signs
crossing their training-set means. On test data, later forecasts beat the twin’s own hour-6 fore-
casts of the same windows in all 12 settings (+0.073to+0.153AUROC). On validation data,
controls that withheld or swapped the new hours traced the gain to the patient’s own measure-
ments. Without refitting, the model kept its gain on a second database (8 of 9 settings,+0.025
to+0.114AUROC) in a prespecified evaluation of the previously analyzed MIMIC-IV test split.

the treatmentAby intervention.b, Data and design. Three harmonized databases are placed on an hourly
grid of 161 input channels (41 physiological, 120 treatment; Methods), and bars give each database’s stays
in the experimental cohort (Table 1). ICare-DT is trained on eICU-CRD (eICU in the panel), and every
analysis uses eICU-CRD except one registered read of the previously analyzed MIMIC-IV test split. That
read scored the two prediction results (synchronization and the clinical-endpoint probes), with disclosed
secondary outcomes (Supplementary Note 7). MIMIC-III appears only in earlier transfer analyses that
were not registered (Supplementary Note 8). A semi-synthetic generator writes injected responses onto
real eICU-CRD records. Its generated dataset passed a locked realism audit (Fig. 4b).c, Inputs. A
causally masked Transformer encodes the patient historyH t (physiology, laboratory values, treatments,
measurement mask and static covariates) into the patient statez t.d, Readouts. The joint competing-
risks forecast gives, for each of four vital signs, the probabilities that a crossing of the training-set mean,
live discharge from the unit or death comes first, 1 to 48 hours ahead. Clinical-endpoint probes read the
state for four clinical endpoints (in the panel, ICU death is death in the unit and kidney injury is acute
kidney injury; Methods). The counterfactual rollout generates the next hour under a chosen action and was
evaluated only on a historical benchmark (Fig. 4a). State synchronization re-reads newly recorded hours
with frozen weights.e, Causal query, the intended use of a response module. Predicted courses under

cant). To test response prediction, we built a benchmark that replaces the treatments in real
records with simulated doses and injects responses of known size, visible only at measure-
ment times. Ridge models supervised with injected effects recovered them from real records
only through frequently measured variables (heart rate) read at their measurement times. We
asked standard learners to predict these effects for a dosing regime no patient had received.
No standard learner outperformed predicting zero effect at an out-of-support query. When told
how the simulated responses were generated, a separate learner recovered the effects from

the benchmark. The action-conditioned rollout scored on it had a clock defect. It wrote each
transition sample into the row of the action that conditioned it, although the transition adapter had
been trained to predict physiology one hour after that action. Generated physiology therefore led
its time index by at least one hour, and by more where the adapter carried persistence through
generated physiology. In deterministic toy tests (Supplementary Note 3), the defect inflated the
mean response over the benchmark’s 12-hour window by factors of 1.00 to 1.38. Its effect on the
historical readouts was not estimated. We report those readouts as run, and no positive finding
of this paper rests on them.
evidence_fragments.extractor_or_reviewer: Phase E repair reviewer (direct verification from extracted PDF text)

capability_assessments.rationale: Downgraded from L2 to L1: ICare-DT implements a persistent latent patient state z_t updated hourly by a causally masked Transformer and rigorously evaluates 1-48 h competing-risks forecasting on eICU-CRD and MIMIC-IV (L1). Although an action-conditioned next-hour counterfactual rollout adapter exists, it was evaluated only on an earlier historical semi-synthetic benchmark with a disclosed clock defect (p. 31, Supplementary Note 3 p. 68), performed worse than predicting zero effect (MAE 0.021 vs 0.017, p. 10), and the authors explicitly state no positive finding rests on those readouts and do not use the twin's rollout for individual treatment-effect analyses.

limitations: Twin's own rollout is not used for individual treatment-effect estimation; semi-synthetic benchmark shows standard learners fail out-of-support dosing queries.
Retrospective ICU databases only; no prospective clinical deployment.
Phase E repair verified the disclosed rollout clock defect in the historical benchmark (p. 31, Supplementary Note 3 p. 68) and downgraded formal capability from L2 to L1.

legacy_cells.B: ICare-DT: a digital twin for continuous forecasting of intensive care patients
legacy_cells.C: Yanke Li; Yahang Qi; Yumi Kim; Diego Paez-Granados
legacy_cells.O: ICU deterioration; vital-sign threshold excursions; hypotension; acute kidney injury; hypoxemia
legacy_cells.S: Do patient-specific ICU vital-sign forecasts improve as each patient's new hourly record is assimilated, and can the model recover individual treatment responses?
legacy_cells.T: ICU stays in eICU-CRD (training: 140,473 stays of 97,553 patients; test: 30,099 stays of 20,886 patients); transfer/read analyses also used MIMIC-IV; MIMIC-III CareVue appears only in earlier transfer analyses.
legacy_cells.X: F2 EHR / ICU event & latent patient dynamics
legacy_cells.AI: Hourly ICU EHR time series (41 physiological channels; 120 treatment channels); physiological measurement/observation masks; four static covariates (age, sex, height, weight)
legacy_cells.AJ: Per-hour two-layer MLP encoder with SiLU activations and learned random Fourier features of absolute time; two-layer causally masked Transformer (64-dimensional state; four heads; feed-forward width 256)
legacy_cells.AN: Physiological measurement mask and treatment-channel availability mask are input features; records are placed on an hourly grid and values may be forward-filled.
legacy_cells.AQ: Compared hourly records with real measurement cadence: cadence-aware readers recovered injected heart-rate effects at real cadence, whereas no reader recovered creatinine effects; this evaluates how measurement timing affects recoverable task evidence.
legacy_cells.AT: No recursive posterior filter is described; at each hour the frozen network is rerun on the record accumulated through that hour to recompute the state.
legacy_cells.AX: Validation controls withheld new hours or replaced them with a matched other patient's hours. Synchronized forecasts exceeded the other-patient input in all 12 settings (+0.111 to +0.185 AUROC), but the authors say this is necessary, not sufficient, evidence of personalization; information beyond the patient's last value was not shown.
legacy_cells.BI: ICare-DT; ICare-RH (separate candidate response module; not integrated with the ICare-DT state in the registered arm)
legacy_cells.BL: Hourly grid; forecast bins end 1, 6, 12, 24, and 48 hours ahead
legacy_cells.BS: Competing-risk probabilities for each of four vital signs (threshold crossing, live discharge, death); a separate transition adapter generates next-hour physiology under a chosen action, evaluated only on a historical benchmark.
legacy_cells.BT: Four target-specific competing-risk forecast heads; clinical-endpoint probes for ICU death, hypotension, acute kidney injury, and hypoxemia
legacy_cells.BV: Origin-weighted categorical negative log-likelihood for competing-risk labels; clinical endpoint probes use endpoint prediction losses.
legacy_cells.CR: Forecast calibration assessed with mean forecast versus observed rate, calibration intercept/slope, ten-bin reliability tables, Brier score, and log-loss; eICU-CRD hour-48 mean forecasts were 91%–105% of observed rates at 6/12 h and 68%–89% at 24/48 h (without recalibration).
legacy_cells.CX: ICare-DT's own rollout was evaluated only on a historical benchmark, not on the known-individual-effect washout panels; the reported historical rollout had a one-hour clock defect and was not treated as positive evidence of individual-effect recovery.
legacy_cells.DN: eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD); MIMIC-IV; MIMIC-III CareVue; semi-synthetic generated eICU-CRD dataset; three washout panels
legacy_cells.DQ: eICU-CRD: 200,825 stays / 139,362 patients; model training: 140,473 stays / 97,553 patients; test: 30,099 stays / 20,886 patients; MIMIC-IV: 94,458 stays / 65,366 patients (registered test read: 14,211 stays / 9,805 patients); MIMIC-III CareVue: 28,394 stays / 23,692 patients; washout panels: 400 stays each.
legacy_cells.DR: 208 hospitals reported for eICU-CRD; total site count across the three databases not reported.
legacy_cells.DY: Historical action-conditioned rollout: mean absolute error 0.021 versus 0.017 for predicting zero effect over the historical benchmark; authors report a one-hour clock defect and no positive finding rests on this result. Separately, direct forecasts were assessed at 6–48 h horizons (AUROC 0.646–0.820 across 16 threshold-crossing settings).
legacy_cells.DZ: Locked discriminator realism audit: AUC 0.572 for generated dataset (pass threshold 0.75); washout panels AUC 0.714–0.727. The audit failed to flag added measurement noise of 0.15 reference SD and does not establish panel realism.
legacy_cells.EB: The earlier action-conditioned rollout's historical benchmark error was 0.021 versus 0.017 for predicting zero; the rollout had a timing defect, and the paper does not establish treatment-effect recovery by ICare-DT.
legacy_cells.EI: Persistence/last measured value: synchronized forecast exceeded it in 11/12 eICU-CRD test settings (median +0.044 AUROC), but was better in only 1/9 and worse in 2/9 MIMIC-IV settings. Fixed CatBoost on the same hours was stronger on eICU-CRD validation (twin median −0.012 AUROC; worse in 3/12 settings after correction).
legacy_cells.EJ: Causal Transformer, RMSN, CRN, and G-Net were evaluated as treatment-effect sequence/g-computation baselines; none of the 16 scored standard learners outperformed predicting zero effect at the out-of-support query. CRN failed its synthetic positive control and was excluded from scoring.
legacy_cells.EK: Synchronization controls held new hours at hour-6 values or swapped in a matched other patient's hours; treatment-response analyses compared hourly versus real measurement cadence, measurement-hold/missingness corrections, placebo and fixed-schedule controls, and model baselines.
legacy_cells.EL: ICare-DT's historical rollout had a one-hour clock defect; its reported error was worse than predicting zero. ICare-RH failed its real-panel placebo gate (learned lag outside 1–3 h in all discovery folds; placebo predicted-effect spread ratios 1.05, 0.43, and 0.64 versus 0.25 maximum) and was not scored on real records. Twin state alone trailed boosting; MIMIC-IV last-value comparisons were worse in 2/9 settings. No standard treatment-effect learner beat zero at the out-of-support query.
legacy_cells.EO: Uses de-identified research databases; data-use agreements prohibit redistribution of patient-level derived data; database access requires credentialing and compliance with data-use requirements.
legacy_cells.EQ: US Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) safe-harbor de-identification standard is named for eICU-CRD.
legacy_cells.ER: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center IRB approved MIMIC-IV creation/sharing with waiver of informed consent; BIDMC and MIT IRBs approved MIMIC-III with waiver; eICU-CRD use is exempt after safe-harbor de-identification certification.
legacy_cells.FB: Per-hour encoder embeds physiology, treatments, observation masks, and static covariates; a causally masked Transformer maps the record through hour t to a 64-dimensional continuous patient state. The same state supports forecast heads and clinical-endpoint probes.
legacy_cells.FL: Hourly ICU record (physiology, treatment channels, observation masks, static covariates) → two-layer MLP with learned absolute-time Fourier features → causally masked Transformer and 64-D patient state → competing-risk forecasts and endpoint probes; separate transition adapter generates next-hour physiology under a chosen action; no planner or action-selection loop.
legacy_cells.FM: Introduces ICare-DT for hourly state synchronization and continuous ICU forecasting; tests whether patient-specific forecasts improve as records accrue; constructs a measurement-process-aware semi-synthetic treatment-response benchmark and tests recoverability of injected effects.
legacy_cells.FN: On eICU-CRD, synchronized forecasts exceeded hour-6 forecasts in 12/12 settings by +0.073 to +0.153 AUROC; in the registered MIMIC-IV read they did so in 8/9 settings by +0.025 to +0.114. Adding the fine-tuned state to boosting improved MIMIC-IV acute-kidney-injury AUROC by +0.0035 (not hypotension). At real cadence, only cadence-aware readers recovered injected heart-rate effects; no standard learner beat zero at the out-of-support query, and ICare-RH failed placebo checks.
legacy_cells.FO: All data are retrospective and from US hospitals; eICU validation/test, endpoint tuning, and MIMIC-IV splits had prior reads; transfer controls and treatment-response analyses were not repeated on MIMIC-IV. Threshold crossings are not clinical events; synchronization analysis included only stays with hourly target measurements (42.9% of test stays). Washout responses and dosing were simulated, binary exposure does not cover dose response, no query inside the support met overlap criteria, the realism audit missed added noise and does not prove panel realism, and the historical rollout had a clock defect. Prospective clinical evaluation, clinically defined targets, and recalibration remain needed.
legacy_cells.FP: Develop a response module that learns response structure from factual data, passes placebo checks, and recovers injected responses at real measurement cadence before testing against real treatment decisions (for example, by emulating a randomized target trial); prospectively evaluate and recalibrate forecasts at deployment sites; release generator and washout-panel code and registered records.
legacy_cells.FQ: Prior evaluations did not establish that forecasts improve because they assimilate new patient data, and routine records may not contain enough information to learn individual treatment responses because observation timing and treatment are clinically selected.
legacy_cells.FR: Forecast assimilation and retrospective transfer are demonstrated, but not decision benefit, prospective clinical utility, or a complete perception–dynamics–planning loop. Action-conditioned rollout is not causal identification; ICare-DT's rollout was not tested on the individual-effect panels and its historical benchmark had a clock defect. Semi-synthetic realism-pass results do not establish real treatment effects or realistic counterfactual records; treatment-response claims remain unproven, especially outside observed support.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M1 Data adapters & provenance; M3 Belief-state service; M5 Dynamics adapter; M7 Outcome & causal layer
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Separate improved forecast assimilation from treatment-response identification; validate response recovery at real measurement times and under known effects.

The main-text figures/results and relevant table entries were inspected. Supplementary material spans the remaining extracted PDF pages and was not exhaustively read; no unreadable table was encountered. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text.
